verdict.rationale: OpenCode is itself an AI coding agent: users delegate tasks to it in the terminal, desktop app, IDE, via `opencode run`, or through GitHub comments, where it works in a branch and opens a PR. It offers built-in primary agents and subagents (plan, explore) that users switch with Tab or invoke with @ mentions, and community users confirm daily use and praise the subagents. missing for 10: documented reliability on long or nested sessions (users report agents occasionally getting stuck and failing tool calls, especially with local models).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: OpenCode is an open source AI coding agent. It's available as a terminal-based interface, desktop app, or IDE extension.
Ask OpenCode to fix an issue or implement a feature. And it will work in a new branch and submits a PR with all the changes.
Mention `/opencode` or `/oc` in your comment, and OpenCode will execute tasks within your GitHub Actions runner.
You can also manually invoke them by **@ mentioning** them in your messages.
I really like how their subagents work, as a bonus I get to choose which model is in which agent.
